newsitem.title: IRAQ: First oil tanker docks at Iraq's Mina al-Bakr.
newsitem.headline: First oil tanker docks at Iraq's Mina al-Bakr.

text.p: The ultra-large oil tanker Stena Companion docked at Mina al-Bakr on Monday afternoon to be loaded with 2.2 million barrels of Iraqi crude oil, the Iraqi News Agency said.
The Stena Companion is the first tanker to load oil from Iraq's gulf terminal of Mina al-Bakr under the second round of Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.
The agency said shipping authorities were now preparing to receive a second tanker on Tuesday, the Jahre Ventura, which was originally due to dock first.
The Jahre Ventura is now due to arrive on Tuesday to take 2.5 million barrels for U.S. trader Bayoil.
Iraq resumed limited oil exports under the second phase of the U.N. agreement last Wednesday from the Turkish port of Ceyhan.
Three tankers, the Arcadia (Bayoil), New Horizon (Coastal) and the Landsort (Total) have so far exported cargoes of Iraq's Kirkuk crude from Ceyhan.

The pact allows Iraq to sell $2 billlion worth of oil over six months in two equal 90-day instalments and was renewed for a second phase on June 8. Iraq has delayed exports to modify plans for aid distribution.
